title: Launch Catalyst — Ops Cheat Sheet & KPI Loom
content:
Purpose:
Quick, portable launch cheat sheet for short-window feature launches and emergency rollouts. Designed for the product-ops / oncall crosswalk — lightweight, actionable, and copy-pasteable into Slack or the runbook.

Who should carry this: product-ops lead + SRE oncall + release engineer + triage owner.

Top-of-mind KPIs (tracked in morning cadence):
- Request success rate (200s / total): target >= 99.6%
- Median p95 latency (in ms): goal p95 <= 220ms for API route /chat/generate
- Cost per 1k tokens (hosted): baseline $0.95 +/-10%
- Error surface: % of model-variant fallbacks invoked: target < 2%
- Quality regressions: new-revision hallucination rate on eval prompts: < 1.5%
- Business signal: conversion uplift (first 7d) relative to control: target >= +3%

Quick readiness checklist (copy for each day-of):
[ ] Owner assigned for live incident comms (Slack #launch-comm)
[ ] Canary traffic rule set and feature flag deployed (FeatureGate ID)
[ ] Dedicated bursts configured (if traffic surge expected) — Dedicated pool: D-Pool-7
[ ] Auto-fallback policies tested (model fallback matrix validated)
[ ] Observability dash open: latency, cost, token breakdowns, error traces
[ ] Roll-forward and rollback runbooks pinned in runbook header
[ ] Paging list and oncall rotations confirmed for 72h window

Operator quick-actions (if things go sideways):
- If p95 > 350ms for >10m AND error rate rising: reduce canary weight by 50% and trigger A/B revert flag (flag -> off).
- If error rate > 1% sustained for 5m: switch to warm fallback model variant: model:vX-small-quant -> model:vX-medium-quant, notify product and ops.
- If cost per 1k tokens spikes > 30%: temporarily enable token cap (per-user) and throttle non-critical routes.
- If hallucination signal > threshold on live eval prompts: halt new model rollouts, set model back to previous commit hash, open postmortem.

Minimal launch telemetry snapshot (paste into sync post every 30m):
- time: HH:MM UTC
- traffic: total req/min | canary %
- success rate: %%
- p50 / p95 latency: ms / ms
- tokens consumed per min: #
- top 3 error messages: list
- cost burn delta vs baseline: +/-%

Small capacity/cost forecast (very quick heuristic we use during rapid rollouts):
- Baseline (prod steady): 1k req/min -> 30k tokens/min -> cost $28/hr
- 3x spike (expected worst short): 3k req/min -> 90k tokens/min -> cost $84/hr
- Dedicated burst buffer: allocate 2x baseline for 60min -> reserve D-Pool-7 at 2x
Notes: run this table with real token distribution for feature (i.e., if feature adds average 400 tokens vs typical 120 tokens, scale costs accordingly).

Launch owner mapping (fast roster) — copy onto incident page:
- Launch lead: Maya Patel (product-ops) — overall decisions, go/no-go
- Release engineer: Jonah Kim — deploy flags, canary weights, infra changes
- SRE oncall: Priya Raman — latency/error triage, scaling actions
- Observability owner: Luca Moretti — dashboards, trace correlation, APM hooks
- Customer comms: Samira Owens — customer status updates and RM handoffs

Risks + mitigations (fast read):
- Risk: sudden token-cost surge from misrouted traffic -> Mitigation: prebound throttle on secondary routes, emergency billing cap with finance (FIN-ops contact).
- Risk: silent quality regression (low-volume hallucinations) -> Mitigation: include 50 golden prompts in canary traffic; run automated scorer every 10m.
- Risk: config drift between hosted/dedicated -> Mitigation: run the config diff script (ops-config/scripts/diff-config.sh) prior to release.

Open questions (todo before final launch):
- Confirm retention window for per-token telemetry (30d default?) -> ACTION: Luca to confirm with infra logs team (ticket INFRA-1212).
- Do we need an SLA addendum for customers in beta? -> ACTION: Samira to check legal / CS.

Post-launch lightweight retro template (fill within 48h):
- What went well (3 bullets)
- What surprised us (2 bullets)
- Biggest blocker we couldn't automate (1 line)
- Action items (owner + ETA)

Snippets to paste into Slack run channel: 
- "CANARY ALERT: canary weight reduced to X% due to p95 latency > 350ms. Investigating — SRE oncall priya@redwood"
- "ROLLBACK INITIATED: model rollout reverted to vX-2024-11-01 hash abc123. All traffic back to stable."

Mini checklist for customer-facing comms (if customer impact):
- Confirm affected customers list (CS curator -> Samira)
- Draft initial status update: cause / immediate mitigation / ETA for fix
- Escalation: Sales + Legal briefed if > 5 customers impacted or > 4h downtime

Notes to self / shorthand (raw):
- Keep the golden prompt set small (50) but domain representative. Run eval scorer (python scripts/eval_live.py --set golden50)
- If using dedicated pool, ensure isolation tag applied so cost is charged to commitment project
- Confluence doc to link in postmortem: https://confluence.redwood.internal/display/OPS/postmortem-template

Reference quick links (copy into the doc header when sharing):
- Deploy flag console: https://flags.redwood.internal/feature/LAUNCH-XXX
- Canary dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/canary
- Token + cost breakdown: https://console.redwood.internal/costs/token-breakdown

End of cheat sheet — keep this file small, copy into the runbook for each launch.

Revision log:
- 2024-11-05 Maya Patel: initial draft, added fast heuristics and checklist
- 2024-11-20 Jonah Kim: added operator quick-actions, capacity heuristics
- 2024-12-03 Priya Raman: added rollback triggers and telemetry snapshot format
